question: Will the US conduct a military strike inside Iranian territory on October 1 or October 2, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Reference class: 2-day windows during the 2026 Iran war since the July ceasefire collapse. US strikes hitting Iranian territory occurred on roughly 12 of the last 60 days, heavily clustered into multi-day waves (late-July 11-13 night run; Sept 1-8 wave), implying ~30% of randomly chosen 2-day windows contain one. Conditioning: as of Sept 19 GlobalSecurity records a twelfth consecutive operational period with no announced US strike ashore and a two-sided fire pause since ~Sept 8-9, which lowers the near-term rate; but the window is 9-11 days out, long enough for the lull to break, and the historical inter-wave gap (late-July wave -> Aug 30/Sept 1 wave) is about four weeks, putting a next wave near late Sept/early Oct. Escalation signals (Trump's 'big decision', Iran's military warning the US is preparing to resume, a tanker struck Sept 21, Hormuz still closed) roughly offset de-escalation signals (UNGA week diplomacy with Gulf leaders and Qatari mediation, a pivot to economic pressure, Trump framing the war's end around the November midterms). No human prediction market matches this contract's terms, so no crowd anchor. Landing just under the unconditional base rate.
calls.dossier:
RESOLUTION INSTRUMENT: resolves off credible reporting (plus the 'List of attacks during the 2026 Iran war' Wikipedia page) that US forces hit a target located ON Iranian sovereign territory — land, territorial waters, or airspace — dated Oct 1 or Oct 2, 2026 Iran local time. Does NOT resolve off: US strikes on vessels in international waters, US strikes in Iraq/Yemen/Gulf states, interceptions of Iranian missiles/drones, blockade boardings, or Israeli-only strikes. Joint US-partner strikes count if US participation is reported. Note the Wikipedia list page is flagged incomplete and appears sparsely updated for post-March events, so credible-source reporting will likely do the work.

STATUS-QUO OUTCOME: no US strike on Iranian territory on those two specific days (the default given the current lull), i.e. NO.

EVIDENCE — CURRENT TEMPO
- GlobalSecurity Day 204 update (19 Sep 2026): 'no American or coalition strike on Iranian territory ashore was announced between the 18 and 19 September cutoffs' — the twelfth consecutive operational period without an announced strike ashore; no new CENTCOM press release in the window; CENTCOM public output focused on maritime blockade reporting.
- Same source: 'the destruction of the two IRGC boats on 14 September remains the most recent announced American kinetic action.' Reporting elsewhere places US action against IRGC boats in the Bandar Abbas area; the boats' precise legal location (Iranian territorial waters vs international) is not specified in what I found.
- GlobalSecurity Day 203/204: Iran's side of the pause is in its ninth/tenth day with no Iranian ballistic-missile or drone attack on any host state.
- iranwarlive.com tracker (20 Sep 2026, Day 205): status 'WAR RESUMED'; no ceasefire in force; live US naval blockade of Iranian ports; Hormuz closed by Iran.

EVIDENCE — WAVE STRUCTURE / BASE RATES
- Base rate over ALL days since the July ceasefire collapse (Jul 22 - Sep 21, ~60 days): roughly 12 days carried a reported US strike on Iranian territory (late-July consecutive-night run; Aug 30 Larak Island; Sep 1; Sep 5; Sep 7-8; Sep 14 boats) — about 1 day in 5, but clustered, not spread.
- Base rate CONDITIONAL ON a wave being active: strikes run consecutive nights — CENTCOM announced an 11th consecutive night on 21 Jul 2026 (Al Jazeera) and a 13th consecutive night on 23 Jul 2026 (US News/Reuters). Within an active wave, consecutive-day continuation is the norm.
- Base rate CONDITIONAL ON a lull: August 2026 saw a roughly month-long gap between the 29 Jul wave and the 30 Aug limited strike — extended zero-strike stretches are an established mode of this war.
- Inter-wave spacing observed: late-July wave -> 29 Jul large wave -> ~1 month gap -> 30 Aug limited strike -> 1 Sep ~100-target wave (largest since 29 Jul) -> 5 Sep and 7-8 Sep tanker strikes -> lull from ~8-9 Sep. The current lull, measured from the last ashore strike, is about 13 days as of Now.
- GlobalSecurity Day 187 (2 Sep 2026) characterizes US doctrine as a recurring 'mow the lawn' cycle: officials said the 1 Sep wave 'bought at least a month'; Trump quoted as 'We waited until it was almost built and then we hit it' — i.e. pauses are deliberate and timed to Iranian reconstitution, not to diplomacy.

EVIDENCE — ESCALATION DIRECTION
- Trump, 17 Sep 2026 (Axios, via Times of Israel/Breitbart): 'I have a big decision coming up. Do I want to go in and annihilate them or do I not?'; reported to be weighing a return to large-scale strikes.
- Al Jazeera, 21 Sep 2026: Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters says it has information the US is preparing to resume strikes; warns of retaliation against US bases and that host countries would be 'considered complicit.'
- Okaz (20 Sep 2026): Trump returned early from Camp David without explanation; US warnings to citizens in the region, a reported US military options review, and reported activity at Iranian nuclear facilities; article states no official confirmation that any 'decisive strike' has been decided.
- TAG24 newsticker (21 Sep 2026): a tanker entering the Persian Gulf was hit by a projectile, two crew lightly injured (UKMTO); Iranian officials say Hormuz stays blocked until US conditions are met; Iran warns any new attack brings 'continuous, effective' strikes.
- Historical trigger pattern: the 1 Sep wave followed IRGC attempts against shipping and US personnel; the 5 Sep tanker strikes followed Iranian missile attempts on a US Navy warship. Attacks touching US forces or shipping have preceded US strikes within days.

EVIDENCE — DE-ESCALATION DIRECTION
- UNGA high-level week runs 22-26 Sep (plus 28 Sep). Trump was set to meet the leaders of Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait and Oman on the sidelines on Tue 22 Sep, with the Iran war central. Iranian President Pezeshkian leads a delegation to New York; the administration granted visas to senior Iranian officials (NBC).
- Reporting cited in the question background indicates a 'day-after' plan would be finalized only after the November US midterms.
- Trump, 9 Sep 2026 (Al Jazeera/Time): the war 'will end right after the midterms'; he also claims Iran 'wants to make a deal so bad.'
- Qatar has initiated mediation to end the conflict and reopen Hormuz (per the September strikes Wikipedia article); Iran conveyed conditions through Qatar around 19-20 Sep. No agreement reported.
- US pressure is currently running through economic instruments: Treasury Secretary Bessent announced all Iranian airlines grounded globally from Wednesday (TAG24, 21 Sep); earlier the administration ran a sanctions-first phase dubbed 'Economic D-Day'; a live naval blockade is in place. Iran's rial at ~2,311,000/USD, food inflation 127.5%, crude loadings down ~85%, Brent ~$102 (GlobalSecurity, 18-19 Sep).

calls.reasoning: Reference class: 2-day windows during the 2026 Iran war, split by regime. Unconditionally ~34% of war-days saw a US strike on Iranian soil (Feb 28-May 5 major combat, mid-July's 11 straight nights, Aug 30, Sept 1-7), giving ~40% per 2-day window. But conditioning on the CURRENT regime is decisive: 12+ consecutive operational periods with no announced strike ashore as of Sept 19 (GlobalSecurity OPREP Day 204), and in comparable lull regimes (Aug 1-29, Sept 8-21) the ashore rate is ~1 day in 45, i.e. ~4% per 2-day window. US kinetic action has shifted to maritime interdiction, which the fine print excludes unless reported inside Iranian waters. Three YES pathways: (a) Trump's pending 'annihilate' decision after the Sept 22 Gulf summit producing an active campaign by Oct 1-2 (~12%, discounted because he also says the war is nearing its end, floated ending it after the Nov 3 midterms, and is publicly satisfied with the blockade/economic track); (b) a tit-for-tat retaliatory strike ashore triggered by an Iranian attack, the exact mechanism behind Aug 30 and Sept 1 (~7% for a specific 2-day window); (c) a maritime strike reported as hitting an Iranian island/port or Iranian territorial waters and counted by the resolver (~6%). Compounding gives ~20%, shaded to 18% for the strength of the two-week ashore drought and the mutual de-escalation in tempo. Main counterargument: this war has broken month-long lulls abruptly with days of notice, and the window sits 9 days past a genuine decision point.

Reference class is 'a specific 2-day window drawn during the 2026 Iran war': US ashore-strike days cluster into short waves (Feb 28, May 7, Jul 6-7, Sept 1-7) separated by multi-week lulls (August was quiet enough that Sept 1 was called the 'first clash in a month'), giving roughly a 20% unconditional chance a random 2-day window contains one. Conditioning down: an active lull with Doha/Oman channels, a pivot to economic tools (airline grounding), and reporting that the big decision may wait until after the Nov 3 midterms. Conditioning up: Trump's 'annihilate' decision framed around the Sept 22-23 UNGA Gulf meetings, continued Iranian attacks on shipping (tanker hit Sept 21), and the standing tanker-for-tanker policy — and once a wave starts it runs many consecutive nights, so any window inside a wave is near-certain YES. Roughly 30% that a wave begins in the ~11 days before Oct 2, ~65% that it covers Oct 1-2 with a territorial strike, plus a few points for one-off retaliation or a boat/tanker strike credibly located in Iranian territorial waters.

calls.reasoning: Status quo is a ~14-day lull with no US strike on Iranian soil since the Sept 1-7 wave, plus a two-sided fire pause since Sept 8-9; confirmed nothing ashore on Sept 20-21. Conditioning on the lull regime (~1 ashore day in ~45) gives ~4% per 2-day window, but the regime is not stationary: Trump's pending 'annihilate' decision, the Sept 22 UNGA Gulf-leaders meeting, and this war's 11-day lull-break latency (Aug 19 pivot -> Aug 30 strike) map onto almost exactly Oct 1. Against that: Trump says the war is 'hopefully' nearing its end, is pleased with the blockade, floated ending it after the Nov 3 midterms and would not say whether he decides before them; Qatar/Oman mediation is live and pressure has shifted to economic tools (global Iranian airline grounding from Sept 23). Three paths: decided resumption running on Oct 1-2 (~13%), one-off retaliation ashore triggered by continued Iranian shipping attacks (~4%), and a tanker-for-tanker strike near Kharg/the Iranian coast reported inside Iranian territorial waters and counted (~5%). Sums to ~23%.
calls.reconciliation: Five checks run. (1) 'US strike Iran September 21 2026 CENTCOM Iranian territory' returned nothing later than the Sept 1 wave and the early-Sept tanker strikes — no evidence the ashore lull broke on Sept 20-21; this settles against Run 1's near-unconditional 30%. (2) Trump/UNGA check confirmed the Sept 22 Gulf-leaders meeting and, decisively, that Trump declined to say whether he would decide before or after the November midterms — the decision is real but its timing is unresolved, so Run 1's assumption that a wave naturally falls near early October is not supported, while Run 2's treatment of the lull as near-stationary ignores a genuine 11-day-latency precedent (Aug 19 pivot -> Aug 30 strike) that maps Sept 22 onto Oct 1. (3) Location check on the tanker strikes returned CNN/Al Jazeera/NPR reporting that the Sept 5 strikes hit tankers 'near Iran's Kharg Island' and in the Gulf of Oman — Kharg-anchored vessels sit inside Iranian territorial waters, so Runs 2/3 are right that this is a live YES pathway worth ~5 points and Run 1 was wrong to ignore it; the discount is on whether reporting characterizes the location precisely enough for the resolver. (4) Market check: the Polymarket 'US strikes Iran by October 3' and 'US next strikes Iran on…' ladders are the February 2026 series, already resolved — the October rungs show 0% because they were never reached, not because anyone prices October 2026; Kalshi's live Iran books are Hormuz-closure and nuclear-deal only; the Manifold contract is Iran-strikes-US-base, opposite direction. No valid anchor found, nothing blended. (5) Came back empty: no reporting of the Sept 22 meeting's outcome (it has not occurred), no announced US deadline or scheduled decision falling on or near Oct 1-2. Remaining dispute is pure judgment — how much to discount the lull for a known upcoming decision point. I take Run 2's conditioning framework but not its near-static application of it, landing above Run 2 and Run 3 and below Run 1.
